posts.title: LEGO Star Wars 2027 News - EVERYONE PLEASE READ FIRST POST
posts.text: This thread collects everything we know about 2026 LEGO Star Wars sets: If you have news, substantiated rumors (you have a source that you can name or allude to), or other information regarding new 2027 sets, please post it here. Nothing else. This is not for posting vague hints and toying with people. This is not a discussion thread, that can be found here. This IS your warning! If you have questions about what belongs in this thread, please PM MKJoshA, Brickdoctor, Clone OPatra, or another Moderator. This is for news and news only. If you choose to post fabricated information; you can expect to be banned! It's not worth the fifteen minutes of internet fame. This is for news and news only. This topic is for 2027 news, not 2026, and not 2028. We will make a new topic when we feel it is necessary. If your post was on the boards, and now it's not...there is a good chance it was either hidden or moved. Off topic posts, placing info in the wrong thread, or a request from LEGO to remove something; these are all possible reasons why something may have disappeared. Thank you! Eurobricks Star Wars Forum Spoiler Policy With regards to upcoming sets and rumors: Read at your own risk. This is a topic about potential items to be released. If you do not want to know, stay out of these forums!!! With regards to spoiler tags: these are not required and we will not force anyone to use them. That being said, I'm sure if you did use them, the community would be a much happier place! Please be respectful of others. If a member used a spoiler tag, their intention was to keep something quiet; it was a courtesy to others. If you choose to comment on the contents of that spoiler tag, please refrain from publicly mentioning what the contents of the spoiler were!!! With regards to movies or shows: We feel that two weeks from the release date is an ample amount of time for most people to view a movie. Once a movie or episode is released, we the staff, will do all we can to curb the usage of spoilers in any of the topics in the Star Wars forum for two weeks. If you do not see the movie or episode within two weeks, then you read here at your own risk. This is the policy in the Star Wars forum, going forward. If you did not agree with us in the past, so be it. From this point on, we will not police the threads unless something becomes an issue. We ask that members not mini-mod (directly telling other members how to behave ) in the thread and tell others to use spoiler tags. If something is a problem, please inform the mods by reporting it. Any questions, please ask in the appropriate thread.

posts.text: Yeah, I thought 2019 was a real strong year. You could get the definitive Slave 1 and the definitive Millennium Falcon in the same year. The Falcon didn't have the ESB cast, but that wasn't a problem when you could get Han and Leia in other sets that year. We got the necessary remake of Kylo Ren's shuttle and Anakin's podracer too. The A-wing and Y-wing weren't anything special, but they weren't bad. Edit, and the Tantive IV. So that was three big classic playscale OT ships, all done to a very high standard, in one year. Never mind that the Falcon was actually an ST set, it counts because the OT minifigs were available in 2019.

posts.title: Modular Building Sets - Rumours and Discussion
posts.text: A newspaper press sounds like a great idea for a future modular especially since a lot of them are already built in an old-fashioned style. The Police Station already contains a newspaper stand, Detective's Office contains a smaller one, the newspaper part appears in Assembly Square, and newspapers are sold at the Corner Kiosk GWP. This would all make one tie in well. You could probably reference some of those other modulars with it. With how commonly suggested of an idea it is, they could have done one years ago. As I quoted above, they had also proposed a Shopping Street "with an aisle down the middle," but didn't go ahead with it as it was too difficult to fit in as many businesses as they wanted to. This ended up being similar to the one from 2026. If that was not a coincidence, I'm hoping in the same way there will be a printing press modular in the future.

posts.title: LEGO The Legend of Zelda - Discussion and Speculation
posts.text: Pfft. Fake fan. (j/k) Make no mistake, there is a TON of stuff in the Wild era that would make absolutely fantastic sets! The Divine Beasts, Guardians and Constructs, towns and ruins, the exotic foliage of the Depths, Stables, giant monsters. But there's a ton of stuff from other games that would be good too! I want the King of Red Lions and Tetra's ship. I want a Minish village. I want a modular Castle Town that can be tweaked to represent its various incarnations. I want the Spirit Train. I want excuses to include all the iconic recurring characters (and the fun new ones too). posts.title: Lego Ideas
posts.text: Hi everyone! I’m a product design student from Hungary, and I’m currently working on a project exploring how LEGO builders find inspiration when they run out of ideas or want to create something new from the bricks they already have. My goal is to design a playful, physical tool that encourages creativity, helps people overcome creative blocks, and inspires them to discover new possibilities with their existing LEGO pieces — especially older bricks that might otherwise remain unused. I know there are already apps and online platforms that provide building ideas, but I’d like to explore an alternative that reduces screen time and encourages hands-on experimentation, playful thinking, and unexpected combinations. I’d love to hear about your experiences! What do you usually do when you don’t know what to build? Do you use apps or websites for inspiration, or do you prefer experimenting on your own? Have you ever created something completely unexpected from random LEGO pieces? What would help you come up with new ideas? I’ve also put together a short questionnaire for my research. If you have a few minutes, I’d really appreciate it if you could fill it out! https://forms.gle/asBtrgEadbqgFKsk9 Thank you so much for your help and for sharing your creativity! forms.gle

Lego Blockly: Graphical Common Programming Environment Web App (Using Intuitive Blockly) for All Lego Robotic Platforms.
posts.text: I was searching on bricklink to buy an RCX USB Tower and Powered Up Remote handset few weeks ago and found an Interface A not too expensive in B-C Canada. I just finished my ESP32 setup using @Toastie's configuration mostly. I installed a 8-Led board even if it's not really necessary but it's a nice addition for testing without Int.A. However, I do not plan to remove the ESP32 from the Int.A anytime soon :-) I used a 30-pin ESP-WROOM-32 devkit-1. Because the GPIO's aligns well with the Int.A IDC receptacle (As suggested by @Toastie setup). I didn't have IDC Connectors so I used some PCB 2.54 mm Header female pins. I glued 3 pins header for the top row pin 1, 3, 5 needed for 3.3v and gnd. I use a buck-boost DC-DC converter TPS63802 to use the 3.7v from the Int.A always-ON port to power 5V to the ESP32. Final setup: Only main power to the Int.A is required, I'm using BlueTooth to connect to Lego blockly (BT Virtual Com Port) so no need for data cable to computer.

posts.title: LEGO The Legend of Zelda - Discussion and Speculation
posts.text: I sort of feel like part of the challenge with expanding The Legend of Zelda to a full theme is that compared to many other licensed themes, Zelda games have a variety of visual styles that don't necessarily mesh with each other, making sets based on different games not complement each other quite as well. Like, Star Wars has sets based on multiple movies, shows, etc., but outside of the brief flirtation with a less traditional style for Clone Wars minifigures, you can put Star Wars characters and ships from any movie or show together without them clashing too much. Same with Mario—most modern Mario games have enough visual similarity that you could pair sets or characters based on any game from the past two decades without them looking too out of place. Zelda is a bit more stylistically siloed—apart from the Smash Bros. crossovers that deliberately pair Toon Link from the Wind Waker-era games with versions of Link from Twilight Princess, Skyward Sword, or Breath of the Wild, you rarely see games with different styles juxtaposed. That's less of an issue for adult-targeted display sets than it is for a full retail theme, where one of the main benefits is encouraging buyers to buy multiple sets that complement each other (as well as, for Lego, being able to reuse figures between multiple sets). That's probably not a totally insurmountable issue, but it does sort of add a wrinkle to the usual benefits of a full, ongoing play theme.
